title: How Dhurandhar's Risk-Sharing Model Made Ranveer Singh a Bigger Winner
excerpt: Producer Jyoti Deshpande reveals that Ranveer Singh and director Aditya Dhar took smaller upfront fees with backend deals, turning the Rs 3,200-crore franchise into a template for Bollywood's new economics.
body:
• Ranveer Singh took a smaller fixed fee with a profit-sharing backend deal for the Dhurandhar franchise, according to producer Jyoti Deshpande
  • Director Aditya Dhar followed the same model, receiving a significant upside when the films became blockbusters
  • The franchise's production budget nearly doubled from initial estimates as one film expanded into a two-part duology
  • The Dhurandhar films have grossed over Rs 3,200 crore worldwide, making it the second-highest-grossing Indian franchise of all time

When Jio Studios co-producer Jyoti Deshpande sat down to assemble the Dhurandhar franchise, the biggest question wasn't who would star in the R&AW espionage thriller — it was how to structure deals in an industry where bloated star fees regularly sink projects before they reach audiences.

The answer, Deshpande revealed in an interview with ET Digital, was a model that aligned everyone's financial fortunes with the film's performance at the box office.

Smaller Fee, Bigger Upside

"In Dhurandhar, Ranveer came with a smaller fixed fee and a backend deal, and therefore benefited from that arrangement," Deshpande said. "The same was true for Aditya, who also came in with a smaller fixed fee and a backend. He ended up making a significant upside along with us. That's how you distribute both the risk and the reward."

https://x.com/ranveersrebel/status/2083099530619228663

The arrangement was a departure from the traditional Bollywood model, where top-tier actors command Rs 50-100 crore upfront regardless of a film's performance. Singh reportedly received Rs 30-50 crore in fixed remuneration, well below his market rate, while wagering on the film's commercial potential through profit-sharing.

Director Aditya Dhar, who co-produced the franchise with brother Lokesh Dhar under B62 Studios alongside Jio Studios, made the same bet. It paid off spectacularly.

A Budget That Doubled

What began as a single feature film spiralled into something far more ambitious during production. Principal photography ran from July 2024 to October 2025 across locations spanning Punjab, Maharashtra, Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, and Bangkok.

"On Dhurandhar, we went all in," Deshpande said. "The film ended up being made for almost double the amount we had initially set out to spend. Of course, we eventually ended up with a two-part film, so it became a journey. In the end, all of us went laughing to the bank."

"The box office opening has nothing to do with stars in it because it's a two-day game. Even if you're able to collect for two days, if the film is not good, no matter what, it just tanks."

— Jyoti Deshpande, Jio Studios

The combined budget for both parts came to approximately Rs 255 crore. Against that investment, the returns were extraordinary.

Record-Breaking Returns

Dhurandhar debuted in theatres on December 5, 2025, and grossed Rs 1,307 crore worldwide. Its sequel, Dhurandhar: The Revenge, released on March 19, 2026, surpassed its predecessor with Rs 1,790 crore globally. The combined haul of over Rs 3,200 crore makes the duology the second-highest-grossing Indian franchise of all time.

For Singh, the backend deal transformed what would have been a standard payday into potentially the most lucrative project of his career. For Dhar, it cemented his trajectory after the success of Uri: The Surgical Strike, with the franchise earning critical attention for its ensemble cast — including Sanjay Dutt, R. Madhavan, Akshaye Khanna, and Arjun Rampal — and for its ambitious depiction of India's covert intelligence operations.

A Template for the Industry

Deshpande has positioned the Dhurandhar model as a blueprint for an industry grappling with escalating costs. Her argument: content, not casting, drives sustained box-office performance.

She pointed to other recent Jio Studios releases that succeeded without traditional marquee power. Stree 2 became 2024's highest-grosser before Dhurandhar surpassed it, while Laapataa Ladies earned critical acclaim and represented India at the Oscars.

With hints of a third Dhurandhar instalment in the pipeline — Deshpande has teased a year-end surprise — the franchise's financial architecture may prove as influential as its storytelling. In an industry where a Rs 200-crore flop can sink a studio, sharing risk may become the new default.
